key.decision_why: The fix itself is still the same two-file scheduled-message change, so the first card is not wrong in substance, but the triager needs to know the author's force-push broke the branch and pulled in 121 unrelated files.
key.action_why: laurynmm closed the PR unmerged on 2026-10-05 because it did not follow the contributing guidelines and was not on track to be mergeable.
changed: The author force-pushed twice and squashed the six earlier commits, including a merge commit, into one commit titled 'scheduled messages: Preserve delivered state after notification failure.'
The author says the PR description was updated, for example to explain that there is no filed issue.
still_missing: The squash/rebase is broken: the diff grew from +46/-11 in 2 files to +4994/-5409 in 123 files, mostly unrelated main-branch changes (pnpm-lock.yaml, web/src/*, templates, version.py, etc.).
The PR still does not follow the reviewable-PR guide the maintainer pointed to, because one commit should contain only the intended change.
There is no linked issue and no chat.zulip.org discussion for this self-found bug.
The author has not tested locally because the dev environment is not provisioned, and relied only on CI.
The author's open question about other code that reads ScheduledMessage.failed/delivered is still unanswered.
key.reply_ask: Tell the author that the force-push pulled about 120 unrelated files into the PR, so it cannot be reviewed; ask them to reset the branch so it contains only the scheduled-message fix and test, and to follow the contributing guide (including discussing unfiled bugs first) before asking for review again.

must_have.fact: Says the PR grew from +46/-11 in 2 files to +4994/-5409 in 123 files after the force-push, with mostly unrelated files from main, so the squash/rebase went wrong.
Says the maintainer's request to follow the reviewable-PR guide is still not met, despite the author's claim that the commit is clean.
Recommends not handing the PR off for maintainer review: keep 'not ready' or close, rather than removing the label or assigning a reviewer.
Notes that the PR has no linked issue or prior discussion, comes from a first-time contributor with no merged PRs, and was not tested locally.
